# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Homkham_2019_efavirenz"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Homkham_2019_efavirenz"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0216868> (PLoS One, open access)

Homkham 2019 links the individual average efavirenz concentration of HIV-infected
Thai children to the time course of their HIV-1 RNA load and CD4 cell count with
a three-state target-cell viral-dynamics model. Efavirenz inhibits the infection
rate `beta` through an Imax function of the individual average concentration
`Cav`, and the inhibition at a child's own `Cav` and `IC50` is the paper's
inhibitory score ISEFV (Eq 5). The paper then shows that an ISEFV below 85%
predicts virological failure while the mid-dose concentration C12 does not.

There is no efavirenz concentration state in the model. `Cav` was computed from
each child's individual clearance in the previously published population PK
model of the same cohort (Homkham 2015, Pediatr Infect Dis J 34:1214) and enters
here as the covariate `CAV` (mg/L), constant from the start of treatment and 0
before it.

# Population

87 HIV-1-infected, antiretroviral-naive children (51% boys) from the Program for
HIV Prevention and Treatment (PHPT) Observational Cohort in Thailand (NCT00433030)
who started first-line efavirenz with zidovudine (57) or stavudine (30) plus
lamivudine (84) or didanosine (3) between May 2002 and March 2010 (Homkham 2019
Table 1 and Results). At treatment start the median age was 8 years (IQR 5 to
10), body weight 17 kg (14 to 23), HIV-1 RNA load 5.1 log10 copies/mL (4.6 to
5.4) and CD4 count 71 cells/mm3 (23 to 262). Efavirenz was dosed once daily by
the US FDA weight bands, median 13.9 mg/kg. Median follow-up was 24 months; 443
HIV-1 RNA loads and 447 CD4 counts were analysed.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Homkham_2019_efavirenz")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source; the table
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(target)` | `lambda - d*T - I(t)*beta*T*V` | Eq 1 |
| `d/dt(infected)` | `I(t)*beta*T*V - delta*T*` | Eq 2 |
| `d/dt(virus)` | `p*T* - c*V` | Eq 3 |
| `inh` | `1 - Imax*Cav/(IC50 + Cav)` | Eq 4 |
| `target(0)`, `infected(0)`, `virus(0)` | `c*delta/(beta*p)`, `c*VL0/p`, `lambda*p/(c*delta) - d/beta` | Methods, paragraph after Fig 1 |
| `isefv` | `100*Imax*Cav/(IC50 + Cav)` | Eq 5 |
| `lkin` (lambda) | 89.2 cells/mm3/month | Table 2 |
| `lkout` (d) | 0.1 /month | Table 2 |
| `lbeta` (beta) | 6.7e-6 mL/copy/month | Table 2 |
| `ldelta` (delta) | 15.2 /month, fixed | Table 2; Results (Perelson 1996) |
| `lp` (p) | 6.5e4 (copies/mL)/(cells/mm3)/month | Table 2 |
| `lc` (c) | 3.3 /month | Table 2 |
| `imax` | 1, fixed | Table 2; Results |
| `lic50` | 0.1 mg/L | Table 2 |
| `etalkin`, `etalkout` | SD 0.6, 0.6; correlation 0.6 | Table 2 |
| `etalbeta`, `etalp`, `etalc`, `etalic50` | SD 1.0, 0.4, 0.5, 2.1 | Table 2 |
| `addSd_log10_viral_load` | 0.7 log10 copies/mL | Table 2 |
| `addSd_target` | 176 cells/mm3 | Table 2 |

Dimensional check of each ODE term (time in months, T and T* in cells/mm3, V in
copies/mL):

| Term | Units |
|------|-------|
| `lambda` | cells/mm3/month |
| `d*T` | (1/month)(cells/mm3) |
| `beta*T*V` | (mL/copy/month)(cells/mm3)(copies/mL) = cells/mm3/month |
| `delta*T*` | (1/month)(cells/mm3) |
| `p*T*` | ((copies/mL)/(cells/mm3)/month)(cells/mm3) = copies/mL/month |
| `c*V` | (1/month)(copies/mL) |

# Untreated steady state

Before treatment (`CAV = 0`) the system starts at the chronic-infection steady
state written in the Methods and must stay there.

```{r steady-state}
mod <- readModelDb("Homkham_2019_efavirenz")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ev_hold <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = seq(0, 36, by = 1), evid = 0L, cmt = "target", CAV = 0
)
hold <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_hold, returnType = "data.frame")

# Closed-form steady state from the typical Table 2 values
lambda <- 89.2; d <- 0.1; beta <- 6.7e-6; delta <- 15.2; p <- 6.5e4; c_v <- 3.3
t0 <- c_v * delta / (beta * p)
vl0 <- lambda * p / (c_v * delta) - d / beta
ti0 <- c_v * vl0 / p
r0 <- lambda * beta * p / (d * c_v * delta)

ss_tab <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("T0 (cells/mm3)", "T*0 (cells/mm3)", "VL0 (log10 copies/mL)", "R0"),
  `Closed form` = signif(c(t0, ti0, log10(vl0), r0), 4),
  `Solved, 36 months` = signif(c(
    hold$target[nrow(hold)], hold$infected[nrow(hold)],
    hold$log10_viral_load[nrow(hold)], NA
  ), 4),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(ss_tab)

# Production and loss balance in each equation at T0, T*0, VL0
flux <- c(
  target = lambda - d * t0 - beta * t0 * vl0,
  infected = beta * t0 * vl0 - delta * ti0,
  virus = p * ti0 - c_v * vl0
)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(flux / c(lambda, delta * ti0, c_v * vl0))) < 1e-12,
  # The ODE solve holds the closed-form state (numeric path, rtol 1e-6)
  max(abs(hold$target / t0 - 1)) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(hold$virus / vl0 - 1)) < 1e-4,
  # Table 2 values reproduce the cohort's median baseline viral load
  # (Table 1: 5.1 log10 copies/mL); a transcription slip in lambda, p, c or
  # beta by a factor of 2 moves this by 0.3 log10 or more
  abs(log10(vl0) - 5.1) < 0.2
)
```

The typical child starts at 5.00 log10 copies/mL against the cohort median of
5.1. The typical baseline CD4 count, 115 cells/mm3, is above the cohort median of
71 cells/mm3 (IQR 23 to 262); with an additive residual error of 176 cells/mm3
that gap is well inside the model's stated precision.

# The ISEFV threshold follows from the viral dynamics

On treatment the effective reproductive ratio is `R0 * (1 - ISEFV/100)`. Virus
replication is suppressed when that is below 1, that is when
`ISEFV > 100 * (1 - 1/R0)`. For the typical child that threshold is
`r round(100 * (1 - 1 / r0), 1)`%, next to the 85% cut-off the paper found from
the observed failures with Youden's index (Results). The typical child at the
cohort median Cav of 1.7 mg/L has ISEFV = `r round(100 * 1.7 / (0.1 + 1.7), 1)`%,
against the published cohort median of 95%.

```{r isefv-typical}
isefv_targets <- c(70, 80, 85, 90, 95)
cav_for <- 0.1 * isefv_targets / (100 - isefv_targets) # inverts Eq 5 at IC50 = 0.1
ev_typ <- tidyr::crossing(
  id = seq_along(cav_for),
  time = c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 36, by = 0.25))
) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "target", CAV = cav_for[id], ISEFV = isefv_targets[id])
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, keep = "ISEFV", returnType = "data.frame")

end36 <- typ |> filter(time == 36)
knitr::kable(
  end36 |>
    transmute(ISEFV, CAV = signif(CAV, 3), log10_viral_load = round(log10_viral_load, 2),
              target = round(target)) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "ISEFV (%)" = ISEFV, "Cav (mg/L)" = CAV,
      "log10 HIV-1 RNA at 36 months" = log10_viral_load,
      "CD4 at 36 months (cells/mm3)" = target
    )
)

stopifnot(
  abs(100 * (1 - 1 / r0) - 85) < 3,
  abs(100 * 1.7 / (0.1 + 1.7) - 95) < 1,
  # Below the threshold the virus rebounds above 200 copies/mL by 36 months;
  # above it the load stays far below the 50 copies/mL quantification limit
  end36$log10_viral_load[end36$ISEFV == 80] > log10(200),
  end36$log10_viral_load[end36$ISEFV == 95] < log10(50)
)
```

```{r fig-typical, fig.cap = "Typical-child HIV-1 RNA (left) and CD4 (right) over 36 months at five ISEFV values. The dashed line marks 200 copies/mL, the paper's failure threshold."}
typ |>
  select(time, ISEFV, `log10 HIV-1 RNA (copies/mL)` = log10_viral_load,
         `CD4 (cells/mm3)` = target) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(time, ISEFV)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = factor(ISEFV))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(name = "log10 HIV-1 RNA (copies/mL)", y = log10(200)),
    aes(yintercept = y), linetype = 2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Treatment duration (months)", y = NULL, colour = "ISEFV (%)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. Each virtual child gets a `Cav` drawn from a
log-normal distribution with the published median of 1.7 mg/L and an IQR of 1.3
to 2.2 mg/L (Results), which gives a log-scale SD of
`(log(2.2) - log(1.3)) / 1.349 = 0.39`. HIV-1 RNA and CD4 are observed at the
cohort's six-monthly schedule plus months 1 and 3.

With the Table 2 variances about 6% of random-effect draws have a basic
reproductive ratio below 1, for which no chronic infection exists and the
baseline viral load from the steady-state formula is negative. Every child in
the cohort was viraemic at baseline, so these draws are outside the population
the model describes and are dropped.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2019)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
n_sub <- 200
cav <- exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(1.7), (log(2.2) - log(1.3)) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))))
obs_times <- c(0, 1, 3, seq(6, 36, by = 6))
events <- tidyr::crossing(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "target", CAV = cav[id])

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, returnType = "data.frame")
viraemic <- sim |> filter(time == 0, virus > 0) |> pull(id)
sim <- sim |> filter(id %in% viraemic)

# Residual error from the model's own ini() values
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
sigma <- setNames(ui$iniDf$est, ui$iniDf$name)
sim <- sim |>
  mutate(
    vl_obs = log10_viral_load + rnorm(n(), 0, sigma[["addSd_log10_viral_load"]]),
    cd4_obs = target + rnorm(n(), 0, sigma[["addSd_target"]])
  )
length(viraemic)
```

# Replicates S1 Fig (visual predictive check)

```{r fig-vpc, fig.cap = "Replicates S1 Fig of Homkham 2019: 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of simulated HIV-1 RNA (left) and CD4 count (right) with residual error. Simulated HIV-1 RNA below the 50 copies/mL limit (dotted line) corresponds to the censored values of the published figure."}
vpc <- sim |>
  select(id, time, `log10 HIV-1 RNA (copies/mL)` = vl_obs, `CD4 (cells/mm3)` = cd4_obs) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, time)) |>
  group_by(name, time) |>
  summarise(
    p25 = quantile(value, 0.25), p50 = median(value), p75 = quantile(value, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p25, ymax = p75), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(name = "log10 HIV-1 RNA (copies/mL)", y = log10(50)),
    aes(yintercept = y), linetype = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Treatment duration (months)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The published VPC shows the observed median HIV-1 RNA falling from about 5 to
below the quantification limit by month 6, and the observed median CD4 rising from
under 200 to roughly 750 cells/mm3 by month 36; the simulated percentiles follow
the same course.

```{r vpc-check}
cd4_36 <- vpc |> filter(name == "CD4 (cells/mm3)", time == 36) |> pull(p50)
vl_0 <- vpc |> filter(name == "log10 HIV-1 RNA (copies/mL)", time == 0) |> pull(p50)
vl_12 <- vpc |> filter(name == "log10 HIV-1 RNA (copies/mL)", time == 12) |> pull(p50)
c(cd4_36 = cd4_36, vl_0 = vl_0, vl_12 = vl_12)
stopifnot(
  # Baseline median HIV-1 RNA vs Table 1 (5.1 log10 copies/mL)
  abs(vl_0 - 5.1) < 0.4,
  # Median HIV-1 RNA below the quantification limit by month 12
  vl_12 < log10(50),
  # Median CD4 at month 36 vs the S1 Fig observed median (about 750 cells/mm3);
  # the typical-child asymptote lambda/d is 892 cells/mm3
  cd4_36 > 400, cd4_36 < 1100
)
```

# ISEFV and virological failure (replicates Fig 2B)

ISEFV is computed from each virtual child's own `Cav` and `IC50` (Eq 5). Failure
follows the paper's definition: HIV-1 RNA above 200 copies/mL from month 6,
confirmed at the next six-monthly visit, within the first 3 years.

```{r failure}
visits <- sim |>
  filter(time >= 6) |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(
    above = vl_obs > log10(200),
    confirmed = above & lead(above, default = FALSE)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    isefv = first(isefv),
    # Each child's own suppression threshold, 100 * (1 - 1/R0_i)
    threshold = first(100 * (1 - kout * cvir * delta / (kin * beta * p))),
    failed = any(confirmed),
    t_fail = if (any(confirmed)) min(time[confirmed]) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(isefv < 85, "ISEFV < 85%", "ISEFV >= 85%"))

isefv_summary <- c(
  median = median(visits$isefv),
  quantile(visits$isefv, c(0.25, 0.75)),
  pct_below_85 = 100 * mean(visits$isefv < 85)
)
round(isefv_summary, 1)

fail_tab <- visits |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(n = n(), n_failed = sum(failed), pct = round(100 * mean(failed), 1)) |>
  mutate(published = ifelse(group == "ISEFV < 85%", "15/23 (65%)", "1/64 (2%)"))
knitr::kable(
  fail_tab |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "ISEFV group" = group, "Virtual children" = n, "Failures" = n_failed,
      "Simulated (%)" = pct, "Homkham 2019 (Results)" = published
    )
)

pct_low <- fail_tab$pct[fail_tab$group == "ISEFV < 85%"]
pct_high <- fail_tab$pct[fail_tab$group == "ISEFV >= 85%"]
stopifnot(
  # Cohort median ISEFV vs the published 95%
  abs(isefv_summary[["median"]] - 95) < 3,
  # A low score separates the children who fail: published 65% vs 2%
  pct_low <= 100, pct_high >= 0,
  pct_low - pct_high > 30,
  # Failure is decided by each child's own threshold, not by the 85% cut-off:
  # almost every failing child sits below its threshold and almost every
  # suppressed child above it
  mean(visits$isefv[visits$failed] < visits$threshold[visits$failed]) > 0.8,
  mean(visits$isefv[!visits$failed] > visits$threshold[!visits$failed]) > 0.8
)

# Failing children in the high-score group and their own thresholds
visits |>
  filter(group == "ISEFV >= 85%", failed) |>
  summarise(n = n(), below_own_threshold = sum(isefv < threshold),
            median_threshold = round(median(threshold), 1))
```

```{r fig-km, fig.cap = "Replicates Fig 2B of Homkham 2019: cumulative proportion of virtual children with confirmed HIV-1 RNA above 200 copies/mL by ISEFV group."}
km <- tidyr::crossing(group = unique(visits$group), time = seq(0, 36, by = 6)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(cum = mean(!is.na(visits$t_fail[visits$group == group]) &
                      visits$t_fail[visits$group == group] <= time)) |>
  ungroup()
ggplot(km, aes(time, cum, colour = group)) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(x = "Treatment duration (months)", y = "Cumulative probability of viral replication",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Cav is an input, not a simulated concentration.** The model carries no
  efavirenz PK; `CAV` must be supplied per child. The vignette draws it from a
  log-normal distribution matching the published median and IQR rather than
  from the upstream Homkham 2015 PK model.
* **Random effects.** Table 2 reports Monolix omegas, read as the standard
  deviations of the log-normal random effects (variance = omega^2). The
  'omega lambda,d' entry of 0.6 is read as the correlation between the lambda
  and d random effects; read as a covariance it would imply a correlation of
  1.67, which is impossible.
* **Parameterisation.** The Methods say the initial conditions were
  reformulated to estimate the baseline HIV-1 RNA and CD4 count, with lambda, d,
  beta, delta, p and c derived from them, but no baseline estimates are printed;
  Table 2 reports lambda, d, beta, p and c with their own between-subject
  variability. The model uses Table 2 as printed. With these variances about 6%
  of random-effect draws have no chronic-infection steady state (negative
  baseline viral load); such draws are outside the modelled population and are
  dropped in this vignette.
* **CD4 output.** The paper does not say whether the observed CD4 count is the
  uninfected state T or T + T*. The model observes T. The alternative differs
  by T*, about 5
  cells/mm3 at baseline and near zero on suppressive treatment, which is under
  3% of the 176 cells/mm3 residual SD.
* **Viral-load floor.** `log10_viral_load` floors the virus state at 1e-4
  copies/mL before the log transform so the output stays finite when the virus
  is driven toward zero. The floor is 5.7 log10 below the 50 copies/mL
  quantification limit, so it changes no prediction above that limit and no
  censored-data likelihood.
* **Typographical issues in the source.** Table 2 gives the unit of d as
  cells/mm3/month; Fig 1 and Eq 1 make it a first-order rate constant (1/month).
  Table 1 prints the age IQR as 5 to 6 years and the triglyceride IQR as 85 to
  108 mg/dL around a median of 135; the age IQR of 5 to 10 years from the
  abstract is used.
* **Comparison with the published ISEFV distribution and failure split.** In
  this virtual cohort `r round(isefv_summary[["pct_below_85"]])`% of children have
  an ISEFV below 85% (published 23 of 87, 26%) and the ISEFV IQR is
  `r round(isefv_summary[["25%"]])` to `r round(isefv_summary[["75%"]])`% (published
  86 to 96%). Confirmed failure occurs in `r round(pct_low)`% of the low-score
  group (published 65%) and `r round(pct_high)`% of the high-score group
  (published 2%). The published ISEFV values are empirical Bayes estimates,
  which shrink the very wide IC50 distribution (log-scale SD 2.1) toward its
  median, whereas the virtual children carry the full population distribution;
  children whose own reproductive ratio is high need an ISEFV above 85% to
  suppress the virus (threshold `100 * (1 - 1/R0)`), which is where the excess
  failures in the high-score group come from.
* No PKNCA analysis: the model has no drug-concentration output.
